 The 2027 Tax Brackets Are Worth $384,000 to a 61-Year-Old With $35 Million. Here’s Why.

 A 3.2% inflation adjustment saves a $900,000-earning couple about $3,000 in income tax but shields roughly $384,000 of their $35 million estate from the 40% tax. 
 Higher gift exclusions let a couple with three children and six grandchildren move $360,000 a year out of their estate tax-free. 
 The 3.8% investment surtax threshold isn't indexed, so it hits more investors each year, and a $700,000 Nvidia gain still faces 20% tax. 
 Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor) 
 The IRS published the 2027 tax brackets on Thursday, and the headline figure is 3.2%. That is how far every bracket, the standard deduction, the estate exclusion and about 70 other dollar amounts in the tax code moved up for inflation. For most people the change is worth a few hundred dollars. For a wealthy investor it is worth a great deal more, and the reason is simple: 3.2% of a big number is a big number. 
 Take a 61-year-old investor and his wife. He still works, and between his salary, his bonus and their interest income the couple reports $900,000 of ordinary income a year and takes the standard deduction. They have a $4 million brokerage account, $700,000 of which is unrealized gain in Nvidia, and an estate they put at $35 million. They have three children and six grandchildren. Here is what Thursday's release does for them, line by line, against what it does for a single filer earning $75,000. 
 insta_photos / Shutterstock.com The income tax: $2,894 
 Every bracket edge moved up by about 3.2%. On a joint return the 12% bracket now runs to $104,050 instead of $100,800, the 22% bracket to $218,250 instead of $211,400, the 24% bracket to $416,650, the 32% bracket to $529,100, the 35% bracket to $793,650, and 37% applies above that. The standard deduction for a couple rises $1,000 to $33,200.

 For the couple with $900,000 of income, taxable income after the standard deduction drops from $867,800 to $866,800, and every dollar inside the widened brackets is taxed at the lower rate. The federal bill falls from $243,250 to $240,356. That is $2,894, and it holds for any couple with income above the 37% line: a couple making $1.5 million saves the same $2,894, because once income clears the top threshold, every bracket shift has already been counted. 
 The single filer earning $75,000 in wages gets a $500 bigger standard deduction and a wider 12% bracket. Their bill goes from $7,670 to $7,390. That is $280. 
 The estate tax: $384,000 
 This is the line that matters most, and it is the one the brackets stories bury. The 2025 tax law set the estate and gift exclusion at $15 million per person for 2026 and indexed it to inflation from there. For 2027 it is $15,480,000. A married couple that elects portability on the first death can therefore shelter $30.96 million from the 40% federal estate tax, $960,000 more than in 2026. 
 For the couple with a $35 million estate, that is $384,000 of estate tax that no longer applies, from one year of indexing. It is also $960,000 more they can move into an irrevocable trust during their lifetimes without using any exemption they did not already have. In 2026 their taxable estate above the exclusion was $5 million; in 2027 it is $4.04 million. Each year the exclusion grows with inflation, the line moves again. 
 The gifts: $360,000 a year 
 The annual gift exclusion rises to $20,000 per recipient in 2027, from $19,000, the first increase in two years. A married couple can give $40,000 to each person on their list with no gift tax return and no use of their lifetime exemption. 
 With three children and six grandchildren, the couple can move $360,000 a year out of the estate in 2027, up from $342,000. Over a decade, with the exclusion growing, that is about $4 million that leaves the $35 million estate before the 40% tax ever sees it, and it goes to the family with no tax to anyone. Instead of annual gifts, the same couple can front-load five years of exclusions into a 529 plan for a grandchild in one go, $200,000 per grandchild in 2027, up from $190,000. 
 The Nvidia sale: nothing saved, and a tax that did not move 
 Long-term capital gains have their own brackets, and they moved too. For a couple, the 0% rate now covers taxable income up to $102,100, the 15% rate runs to $633,600, and 20% applies above that. For singles the lines are $51,050 and $563,200. 
 Our investor's $700,000 Nvidia gain stacks on top of $866,800 of other taxable income, which is already past the 20% line, so every dollar of the gain is taxed at 20% in either year: $140,000, and the new brackets save him nothing on it. The wider 15% band only helps a couple whose other income sits below the line. A couple with $400,000 of taxable income selling the same $700,000 position would pay $995 less in 2027 than in 2026. What the release did not change is the 3.8% net investment income tax, which starts at $250,000 of income for a couple and $200,000 for a single filer. Those thresholds were set in 2013 and are not indexed, so the $26,600 of surtax on the $700,000 gain is the same in either year. Inflation moves every bracket in the code except that one, which is why more investors pay it every year. 
 The 0% line is the one a retired investor should notice. A retired couple with no other income can realize $135,300 of long-term gains in 2027, the $102,100 bracket plus the $33,200 standard deduction, and owe nothing in federal tax. In 2026 the figure was $131,100. 
 What else moved for the wealthy 
 The alternative minimum tax exemption rises to $144,700 for a couple and $93,000 for a single filer, and the income where it starts to phase out moves to $1,031,900 and $515,950. For an investor with large incentive stock option exercises or private activity bond interest, that is the figure that decides whether the AMT bites. 
 The cap on the state and local tax deduction gets its own 1% bump to $40,804. The $6,000 senior deduction, the tips and overtime deductions, and the Social Security taxation thresholds of $25,000 and $32,000 did not move at all. Those are fixed in law, not indexed, which is why a retiree on a modest income gets less from this release than a couple at the top does. 
 The bottom line 
 Indexing exists to stop inflation pushing people into higher brackets, and it does that for everyone. But the dollars scale with the size of the numbers. The $75,000 earner keeps $280. The couple with $900,000 of income and a $35 million estate keeps $2,894 on income tax, avoids $384,000 of estate tax, and gives away $18,000 more a year without paperwork. Their Nvidia gain is taxed at 20% either way, and the one line that did not move, the 3.8% investment surtax, is the one that will keep costing them more each year.
